question: At rounds 10 to 20 of the ring of four four-place knots and one five-place knot under the cheapest counts, does the bond-distance table alone give back the junctions and the next round (readers R1, R1', R2), and is the junction graph rigid (3-connected)?

definitions.table: bond_table(stars, m, K): exact distances up to K over bonds with a side of at most m junctions and a connected complement
definitions.R1: the same stages run on to the largest junction size
definitions.R1prime: R1 with cliques in the GF(2) span of the previous stage's junctions discarded (the advisor's linear prune)
definitions.R2: R1's junctions repaired to a legal incidence, kept when their own table equals the given one

public_inputs.run: .venv/bin/python -B check.py gate; .venv/bin/python -B check.py 10 12 14 15 16 18 20 (one process per round); .venv/bin/python -B check.py merge
public_inputs.reused: RING-GROWTH-20261118-001B ring.py, FIRST-KNOT-20261118-001B startlib.py, FRESH-COUNT-20261118-001B freelib.py, BOND-NEXT-JOIN-20261117-001 check_rearrangements.py (closed records, hashes checked on import)

forbidden_inputs: Rounds, parents, history or bit names given to a reader (readers see only the table)
Changing a prediction after a round is read
cheapest_meaningful_control: R0 at round 9 (inside the proved scope) and a mutated round-10 table

predictions.G: brute-force table equality at rounds 1 and 2; R0 exact at round 9; mutant rejected
predictions.F2: no triangle, no pair of junctions sharing two distinctions
predictions.P3: R2 exactly one survivor, the truth
predictions.P4: regrown round equals the true one
predictions.P6: least working horizon = largest junction size - 1

decision_rules.each: as stated in the pre-registration's table; no tolerance

stop_rule: One run per round; read-out; referee hand-off; report.
